pr_body:
Fixed #26826.

**Description**

This PR adds support for zooming via plus/minus in `OrbitControls`.
pr_comments:
Closing. I understand there are pros/cons for solutions based on `event.key` or `event.code` so it's difficult to make a decision. For now, it's up to the application to implement zooming via plus/minus.

FYI: I will not force-push this branch so the code should be available for everyone who wants to implement this approach.

issue_context.title: Add keyboard shortcuts for zoom in and out in OrbitControls.js
comments: I like the idea of support keys for zoom but the suggested change does not work for me. E.g. on macOS the code for plus on the numpad is `NumpadAdd`.

Wouldn't it be even better to replace all usages of `KeyboardEvent.code` with `KeyboardEvent.key`? The second would be more understandable because of comparing with the character instead of some abstract keycode.

`KeyboardEvent.code` is the better default for controls with has been approved in #21056. I don't think there is a need to question this policy. It definitely makes sense for many use cases. There might be exceptions like this issue though.

review_comments: I'm seeing in the demo that it only zooms in when I press "shift + =". Would it be best to use `event.code` and check for `"Minus"` and `"Equals"` so it always works when the appropriate keys are pressed?

What happens when you press a single key? Do you mind sharing screenshots of https://www.toptal.com/developers/keycode when you press `+` and `-`?

I don't think we can use `event.code` because plus and minus exist in so many keyboard layout variations.

When pressing just the `=` key:

```js
{
 "key": "=",
 "keyCode": 187,
 "which": 187,
 "code": "Equal",
 "location": 0,
 "altKey": false,
 "ctrlKey": false,
 "metaKey": false,
 "shiftKey": false,
 "repeat": false
}
```

When pressing `shift + =`:

```js
{
 "key": "+",
 "keyCode": 187,
 "which": 187,
 "code": "Equal",
 "location": 0,
 "altKey": false,
 "ctrlKey": false,
 "metaKey": false,
 "shiftKey": true,
 "repeat": false
}
```

When pressing the `-` key:

```js
{
 "key": "-",
 "keyCode": 189,
 "which": 189,
 "code": "Minus",
 "location": 0,
 "altKey": false,
 "ctrlKey": false,
 "metaKey": false,
 "shiftKey": false,
 "repeat": false
}
```

I'm on a 2021 M1 Macbook Pro keyboard.

Thanks for sharing the data! Overall, I think the result on your computer is as expected. When using `event.key`, the controls react on whatever key or key combination produces a specific value. In this case plus and minus. 

Like mentioned in #26826, there are use cases where a relying on physical key positions is better like when developing a game that requires WASD or arrow keys input. Even if WASD keys are in a different location (e.g. when using AZERTY keyboards), gamers usually play with the same physical keys (see #21055). 

I believe plus and minus needs to be handled differently though because even in context of WASD layouts, plus and minus exists in different variations. So checking for the character via `event.key` should deliver more reasonable results.

I didn't think the +/= key moved around all the much (same spots in QWERTY, AZERTY, DVORAK, etc) - though it looks like it's not in the common spot with a QWERTZ layout, at least.

I guess what I was getting at is that the demo seemed like it had an issue because the key didn't work until I tried shift. I think if I used an app that told me to zoom with - and + I'd think it was broken.

The only other option I can think of is supporting both + and = characters - but I understand that might be unacceptable. Just a suggestion.
I think the user's hands should be able to remain fixed. Consequently, I'd vote for UP/DOWN in combination with one of the option keys -- if possible.

>  I'd vote for UP/DOWN in combination with one of the option keys -- if possible.

I'm afraid this will interfere with existing code in `handleKeyDown()`. Using _only_ the arrow keys means panning, but with either meta/shift/ctrl rotation is triggered. E.g.:

https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/blob/8d71879573ba4b00979d00fed36740f2f9bbce48/examples/jsm/controls/OrbitControls.js#L745-L759
